head: 5de0825
scope: source files only; behavioural tests untouched by rule, architectural tests fair game
note: Round 11 decomposed eleven packages but left twelve source files over 400 lines. Round 12 is the second, stronger pass: every package with a file over that bar, plus the three core files outside auth/. The initial fan-out was eight targets and was scoped too narrowly — sqlite (632), discord (498), matrix (434) and core's presence/tools/config (446/406/401) were all still over it and were launched mid-round.

measurement.method: git ls-tree over packages/**/src/**/*.ts excluding *.test.ts at both revisions; single- and multi-line import statements stripped; everything else counted
measurement.discrepancyNote: The agents' summed self-reports (-25) disagree with the measured figure (-15). Both are defensible; the difference is counting conventions for `export … from` re-export lines and for blank-line separation in new files. The measured number is the one recorded, because it is reproducible from the two revisions without trusting twelve separate hand-counts.

perTarget.note: both structural guards were already location-independent

perTarget.reworked: first attempt widened 15 private fields to public; sent back for a protected chain

perTarget.note: three path-coupled tests designed around rather than re-anchored; two live in other packages

architecturalTests.ruleAtRoundStart: re-anchor by default; delete only with a NAMED behavioural replacement shown failing
architecturalTests.ruleNarrowedMidRound: The rule opened by declaring behavioural tests untouchable, which is too strong outside a decomposition round, and gated deletion twice as hard as writing a test. Narrowed to its actual subject: never let an architectural ratchet drive a structural choice; any agent may move or replace one. The NAME-and-SHOW gate was dropped because 'a new test does not count until you have watched it fail' already covers a replacement. Running agents were not interrupted: their brief already permitted unrestricted re-anchoring, and the round's own scoping independently forbade touching behavioural tests.
architecturalTests.zeroDeletionsNote: No agent deleted an architectural test in either decomposition round. The escape valve every one of them used was re-anchoring, which suggests the deletion gate was never the binding constraint — consistent with narrowing it.

failureModesObservedAgain.detail: shipped-artifacts.test.ts asserted that this plugin never raises NoSuchTopicError and never leaves a room, reading src/index.ts by path. Adding a leaveRoom to park.ts that both throws NoSuchTopicError and POSTs .../leave leaves the old test at 29/29 GREEN. Demonstrated, not hypothesised.

publish-hygiene scanned src/driver.ts for require() calls and drove a per-module case off the result. Moving loadBetterSqlite to a new file drops the run from 13 tests to 12 — the 'better-sqlite3 is an optionalDependency' case stops EXISTING, because the loop iterates an empty array.

export-surface's NAMED_EXPORT pattern never matched `export async function`, so readRetryAfter was invisible to it for eleven rounds. Confirmed by planting an unused `export async function` and watching the fixed scan fail.

A risk clause instructed keeping plaintextCredentialRisks in THAT FILE because net-util's fork registry keys by path. Round 11 had already re-anchored the registry to key by package:name, making the clause stale — a comment enforcing a constraint that no longer existed.

bridge-slack regexes a PRIVATE function's body out of bridge-core/src/engine/presence.ts; bridge-matrix greps four literals out of core's transport/tools.ts and config.ts. A behaviour-preserving move inside core reddens two backend packages, with a message claiming core 'reworded' something it did not. On record since round 9; it shaped this round's cuts rather than being fixed by them.

failureModesObservedAgain.mode: tautology risk introduced BY the re-anchor
failureModesObservedAgain.detail: Replacing a path read with a glob can turn `expect(text).not.toMatch(...)` into `expect('').not.toMatch(...)` if the glob is empty or mis-rooted. The agent added a guard asserting the file list is non-trivial and contains the plugin class. This is the first round where an agent anticipated the failure mode rather than hitting it.

verification.publicSurfaceVerified: per package, from built dist rather than asserted

orchestratorErrors.error: git checkout -- on an applied-but-uncommitted decomposition
orchestratorErrors.detail: Restoring a mutation in the main repo took bridge-postgres/src/index.ts back to the round base, discarding a 792->353 split while its new sibling files survived untracked and typechecked against the old one. Nothing failed loudly. Recovered via `git show :<path>` from the source worktree. This hazard was ALREADY recorded in the protocol after three round-8 agents hit it; knowing it did not prevent hitting it, so the note now names mutation-and-restore as where it lives and extends it to the orchestrator.

orchestratorErrors.error: attributed 31 test failures to code before checking the machine
orchestratorErrors.detail: A matrix rerun showed 31 conformance timeouts against 1 on the previous run. Load average was 47 with kswapd0 at 20% — nine concurrent agents plus test runs had driven the box into swap. All six containers were healthy throughout. On an idle machine the same tree passed 611/611. Two agents independently reported single unreproducible failures in the same window, which is the same cause.

openForRound13: bridge-telegram/src/store.ts is still 418 lines — the one file over the bar.
Test files are now decisively the largest in the repo and are scheduled for their own round; bridge-core's five biggest are all test files.
The capacity scan in stated-bounds.test.ts is path-keyed and already missed eleven exported caps before this round; four more files are now out of its scope.
cli.ts is byte-identical across ten packages but for a class name and two log prefixes, and matrix's copy has now diverged.

Five of thirteen packages have no tsconfig.test.json, so their test trees are never typechecked while CI's comment claims otherwise. Building one for discord surfaces 12 pre-existing errors in 4 test files and zero in src/.

index.test.ts asserts that the trimmed internal buildToolDefs is not re-exported — a symbol that no longer exists anywhere in the repo, i.e. a dead row in a guard whose purpose is noticing dead surface.
